prompt:
Image 1 is the club crest. Images 2 to 5 are photographs of this athlete.

A clean product photograph of a complete Football kit, laid out FLAT and neatly
arranged on a plain light grey surface, photographed from directly above.

EXACTLY ONE of each of these, in the frame, fully visible and not overlapping. A missing
item makes the plate unusable because the poses read the wardrobe from it — and a DUPLICATE
is just as bad, because two shirts leave the poses to choose which one is the kit:
- the shirt, laid flat and face up
- the shorts below it
- BOTH socks, laid out straight
- EXACTLY TWO SHOES IN THE WHOLE FRAME, never two pairs: ONE shoe seen from directly
  above, and the OTHER shoe of that same pair turned onto its side so its full profile
  and its outsole are visible. Two shoes, two views, so nothing about the footwear has
  to be guessed at when the poses are drawn from this plate.
- the ball or implement of Football
- the HELMET, seen from the side with its facemask, and the SHOULDER PADS — the pads are their own separate item, laid flat on the surface in the empty space ABOVE the shirt in the picture, complete with both arched shoulder caps, never tucked inside or underneath the shirt

THE KIT — these are settled decisions, not suggestions. Do not substitute anything.
- shirt: Medium kelly green American football jersey with short sleeves, worn OVER shoulder pads so the shoulders sit wide and square. V-neck collar. The club crest sits CENTRED HIGH ON THE CHEST, just below the collar and ABOVE the number, about the width of a hand. Below it the number 54 large and centred, WHITE with a GOLD outline, and the FULL number 54 again, smaller, on EACH shoulder — both digits on each shoulder, never one digit split across the two. BACK: the number 54 large and centred across the shoulders, WHITE with a GOLD outline, and no crest. No club name, no player name, no sponsor and no lettering of any kind anywhere on it.
- shorts: Full-length matching medium kelly green football pants with integrated thigh and knee pads, and a plain belt at the waist. No lettering.
- socks: Dark green crew socks, plain, with no logo.
- footwear: Plain black American football cleats with a studded outsole and a high ankle collar. NOT sneakers, NOT low soccer boots. The same pair in every shot. PLAIN AND UNBRANDED: no swoosh, no three stripes, no cat, no jumpman, no trefoil, no wordmark — the photographs do not show their boots, so nothing may be added to them.
- equipment: A DARK GREEN American football helmet whose FACEMASK IS THE SAME DARK GREEN AS THE SHELL — green bars, never cream, never white, never grey, never black. The chin strap, the chin cup, the facemask clips and the interior padding are cream white, and a cream white stripe runs over the crown. Plus a plain brown leather American football with white laces. The same helmet and the same ball in every shot.
- Where an item above is described from the athlete's own photographs, any manufacturer's
  logo it genuinely carries stays on it — that is their real clothing.
- The club crest sits on the vertical CENTRELINE of the chest, directly below the collar and directly above the number, with an equal width of jersey to its left and to its right, about a hand's width across. That position is settled and is the same in every frame.

IMAGE 2 SHOWS THIS ATHLETE WEARING THE REAL KIT, and for how
the garments LOOK it outranks everything written above. Copy from it: the cut,
the collar, the sleeve length, where the panels and trim run, the exact colours
of the fabric, the numerals and their outline, the badge and where it sits.
Where the written list and that photograph disagree about an APPEARANCE, the
photograph is right. The list still decides which items belong in the kit, which
are branded, and anything the photograph does not show.
You are photographing THOSE garments laid out flat and clean — not designing new
ones in the same colours.

THE BADGE: take the artwork in image 1 and place it on the shirt UNCHANGED. Treat it as a finished graphic being applied to the garment, not as a subject to redraw or reinterpret: identical outline, identical figure inside, identical colours in identical places, identical proportions. Nothing added, nothing simplified, nothing restyled, and absolutely NO text — no club name, no letters, no word of any kind, not even small. POSITION: the badge sits on the vertical CENTRELINE of the chest, directly below the collar and directly above the number, with an equal width of jersey to its left and to its right, about a hand's width across. Place it exactly there on the shirt as it lies facing you. SIZE: about one twelfth of the shirt's width. It is the ONLY graphic in the entire set.

Hard requirements:
- Everything is BRAND NEW and immaculate: no dirt, no scuffs, no creases beyond the fold
  of laying flat, no wear, no sweat marks. Copy what they wear, never its condition.
- Flat lay from directly overhead. No mannequin, no person, no body, no hanger, no rail.
- Plain light grey surface, evenly lit, soft shadows only. No props, no background objects.
- BRANDING follows the list above, item by item: an item described from the athlete's own photographs keeps the manufacturer's mark it really carries, and an item that came from the sport default is plain and unbranded. Never ADD a swoosh, three stripes, a cat, a jumpman, a trefoil or a wordmark to something the list did not say has one — these marks carry no letters, so "no text" does not cover them and they have to be refused by name.
- No words anywhere: no club name, no player name, no sponsor, no lettering, no woven
  neck label, no care label, no watermark. The squad number appears ONLY if the kit
  description above calls for it, and no other number is invented.
- Sharp throughout, photographic, print quality. Square image.
REVISION — this frame was reviewed and sent back with one correction. It overrides
anything above that contradicts it, and everything else stays exactly as specified:
The garments are PLAIN GREEN: no white or cream cuffs on the sleeve openings, no white or cream panels on the pants, no trim anywhere. The only cream on the kit is the gold-cream outline around the numbers. The SHOULDER PADS lie on their own on the grey surface above the shirt — the shirt is empty, with nothing inside it and no pad showing at its sleeves or collar.
